title: Lefse
instructions: Combine cooked and riced potatoes with melted margarine, salt, and cream.
Cool well before adding powdered sugar and flour.
Roll about 1/2 cup at a time and bake on lefse grill.

title: Potato Lefse
instructions: Boil potatoes (use a dry potato like russets). Rice potatoes while warm.
Measure the potatoes. Add butter, salt, cream, sugar to the warm potatoes.
Let set overnight or until cooled.
Next morning, rice again (2nd time) and add flour.
Take about 1/3 cup and form into a ball.
Flour your rolling board with flour and press down the dough slightly on the board.
Roll into a thin circle like pie crust.
Place on lefse griddle and bake at 450 degrees on one side.
When bubbles appear, turn and bake other side.
Remove from griddle, place in a cloth to keep moist.
When the lefse are completely cold, they can be frozen, wrapped in wax paper and placed in zip lock bags.

title: Lefse
instructions: To riced potatoes, add melted margarine and whipping cream.
Cool.
When ready to roll, add sugar, salt, and flour.
Roll and bake on lefse grill.

title: Lefse
instructions: Mix butter, whipping cream, and salt with riced potatoes before potatoes cool.
To 2 cups of this mixture, add 2/3 cup flour.
Roll and bake.
Repeat until potato mixture is gone.

title: Lefse
instructions: Mix all ingredients together.
Roll and bake on lefse grill.

title: Grandma Bergit's Lefse
instructions: Mix all ingredients together and form into a roll.
Cut into 16 pieces.
Roll each piece as thin as possible.
Bake on lefse grill.

title: Lefse
instructions: Mix riced potatoes with margarine, half & half, and salt.
Add flour and mix well.
Roll and bake on lefse grill.

title: Lefse
instructions: Cook potatoes with their skins on. When done, drain water, peel potatoes and rice.
Mix in butter, half & half, sugar and salt. Cool overnight.
To bake, mix together 2 cups flour with 4 cups potatoes. Roll into log and slice into sections.
Keep unbaked lefse in refrigerator.
Roll dough out and bake on lefse grill (approx. 450 degrees).

title: Selbu Lefse
instructions: Form dough into balls about 1-inch in diameter. Roll as thin as possible.
Cook on dry griddle (475 degrees) turning when one side is lightly browned.
Place finished lefse between damp towels to keep moist. Sprinkle with water to soften if necessary.
For filling: Cream butter. Gradually add heated half & half. Add sugar and mix well.
Spread filling on half of lefse, fold over other half, trim uneven edges and cut into wedges.

title: Lefse
instructions: Mash all ingredients together except flour and let cool.
Cover with paper towels and set in refrigerator only 1-2 hours.
Then add two cups flour; knead a little.
Roll into about 14-15 lefses. No liquid in above recipe.

title: Lefse
instructions: Cook potatoes; then mash and then rice potatoes. Cool.
Measure potatoes (pack into cup when measuring).
Mix in melted butter and half and half with hands. Add flour and salt; mix with hands.
Form into log. Cut off 1/3 cup of dough.
Roll this using a stocking covered rolling pin on a lightly floured, cloth-covered board.
Bake on hot lefse griddle (400-500 degrees). Turn when bubbly on top.
Bake second side until brown spots appear on bottom side.
Remove from griddle, fold into fourths and let cool between tea towels.
When cool, open up completely and refold. Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate or freeze.

title: Lefse
instructions: Cook potatoes. Rice them while hot. Add butter and sugar. Cool to room temperature.
Add flour and salt, mix well, using hands.
Use about 1/3 cup, roll out.
Fry on lefse grill, approx 450˚. One side, flip, then the other.
Take off and cool under towels.

title: Lefse
instructions: Heat milk and water to boil. Add butter, half & half, and salt except potatoes.
Bring to a boil again. Then add potatoes, whipping constantly.
Cool overnight.
Next day, mix together: 4 cups potatoes, 1 1/2 cup flour, 1 T. sugar.
Roll out (about 1/3 cup mixture) thin, bake on lefse grill.

title: Hardanger Lefse
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm water, set aside.
Pour boiling water over rye flour, beat well.
Add milk to cool off flour mixture.
Stir in salt, sugar, shortening and yeast mixture.
Add enough unbleached flour to make a soft dough. Knead about 3 minutes.
Let rise until double, about 45 minutes.
Punch down and form as for buns, about 1 cup each.
Let rise a few minutes and roll with grooved rolling pin or Haring marker (crossed grooved) pin.
Can be baked on an ungreased lefse grill or in a very hot oven (400).

title: Lefse

ingredients.note: 1 can plus enough water to make a cup

instructions: Mix potatoes and sugar together in bowl.
In kettle, put water, milk, evaporated milk, butter and salt. Heat until butter is melted. DO NOT BOIL.
Pour liquid mixture over potato mix and let stand 1 minute.
Mix together with 11 tablespoons oil; mix well.
Divide into 2 bowls (about 5 cups in each). Pat down around sides.
Take double paper towels and lay on top, pressing down on sides. This will take out some moisture.
Set overnight in refrigerator.
When ready to roll, add 2 cups flour to mixture. Mix together and make into walnut-sized balls.
Roll out and grill. Cool in towels.
Start other batch while the first cools.

title: Flat Bread
instructions: Mix like pie crust; add buttermilk.
Make dough into a long roll. Cut into 12 pieces.
Roll out very thin and bake in 350 degree oven on a cookie sheet until golden brown.

title: Flat Bread
instructions: Stir together white flour, whole-wheat flour, cornmeal, and sugar.
Make a well in the middle and add melted shortening or bacon grease and boiling water.
Mix well. You can start making it as soon as cool enough to handle.
Use 1/4 cup dough for each.
Roll like lefse and bake on lefse griddle or on cookie sheets in oven.
Watch carefully as they burn easily!

title: Oatmeal Flat Bread
instructions: Cream sugar and melted butter. Add salt.
Add soda to buttermilk; then add to creamed mixture, alternately with flour.
Add oatmeal.
Roll thin and bake.

title: Flat Bread
instructions: Mix cornmeal, flour, butter, and salt together like pie crust.
Add 2 cups water.
Roll thin. Bake in 375 degree oven.

title: Flat Bread
instructions: Mix like pie crust, add buttermilk.
Make dough in a long roll, cut in 12 pieces.
Roll very thin.
Bake in a 350 degree oven on cookie sheet until golden brown.

title: Oatmeal "Shingle" Bread (Flat Bread)

ingredients.note: to get milk out of oatmeal

instructions: Mix all ingredients together.
Roll thin and bake.

title: Flat Bread
instructions: Mix together like pie crust and add buttermilk.
Roll thin and bake on lefse grill or bake in oven.

title: Potato Flat Bread
contributor: Helga Gamme, Gran, Hadeland, Norway (submitted by Georgia Rosendahl)

ingredients.note: use a mixture of red & white potatoes

instructions: Boil potatoes (unpeeled) and salt until potatoes are done. Peel and cool overnight.
Rice or mash potatoes, put in mixer with flour and sugar and mix until very smooth (a couple of minutes).
Form dough into a firm ball with hands and divide into small patties.
Sift flour on rolling surface and roll each patty in ground whole-wheat flour until thin.
Fry on lefse grill at medium heat.

Helga uses 3 grills; flatbread takes a long time to dry. (Andersons use 1 grill and put the flatbread in a 325-degree oven to finish drying after it acquires a good color and firmness on the lefse grill)

title: Oatmeal Flat Bread
contributor: Karen Moilien Smith, Coon Valley, WI (submitted by Lee Grippen)

ingredients.note: scant, she uses corn & canola by Crisco

instructions: Mix dry ingredients. Add buttermilk and oil.
Make into balls (about golf ball size).
Roll on wax paper over pastry cloth. Flatten with rolling pin into 1/16 – 1/8 inch.
If you have a lefse pin – use it last.
Bake in 350 degree oven about 6 minutes or until light brown.

title: Oatmeal Flat Bread
instructions: Mix all ingredients.
Use 1/4 C. dough for each. (makes about 12 pieces)
Roll as thin as possible.
Bake on lefse griddle or in 375 degree oven.

title: Norwegian Flat Bread
instructions: Mix together graham flour, buttermilk, soda, melted shortening, syrup, and salt.
Add enough flour to roll out. About 2 cups.
Roll thin and bake.

title: Flat Bread
instructions: Mix together like pie crust and add 1/2 cup buttermilk.
Bake in oven, makes 8.

title: Oatmeal Flat Bread
instructions: Mix dry ingredients and cut in shortening.
Stir together sour cream and buttermilk and dissolve soda into mixture.
Roll very thin and prick with a fork if you do not have a prickly rolling pin.
Bake in oven or on a griddle at 375 until edges are golden brown.
It bubbles when baking if the griddle temperature is too hot.

title: Havrekjeks (Oat Crackers)

ingredients.note: find it at Vanberia or Vesterheim or Food Coop

instructions: Soak oatmeal in milk for 2 hours.
To this mixture, add butter, sugar, salt and anise, and mix thoroughly.
Combine the rye and white flour, hartshorn salt and stir until it forms a ball.
Divide into two.
With a grooved rolling pin, roll dough into a 11 x 16 inch rectangle.
Carefully turn on to waxed paper placed on cookie sheet. Prick all over with fork.
Cut into desired size squares.
Bake in middle of the oven at 400˚ for 10-12 minutes.
Cool on rack and enjoy! (This is from Norway)

title: Oat Crackers
instructions: Melt margarine and add remaining ingredients.
Chill one hour.
Roll into thin sheet, cut into 3" rounds.
Bake in 375˚ oven until golden, about 10 minutes.

title: Sirupssnippers
instructions: Bring syrup, sugar and cream to a boil. Add butter and let stand until cool.
Sift baking soda, cream of tartar and spices with part of the flour and add to first mixture.
Stir in enough flour to make a fairly firm dough. Use as little flour as possible.
Knead the dough until smooth and pliant. Cover and chill until the next day.
Roll out dough as thin as possible, and cut into traditional diamond shapes.
A krimpcut tool will give the traditional patterned edges.
Press a 1/2 scalded almond, cut lengthwise, in the center of the cookie.
Place on greased cookie sheet; bake in 350˚-375˚ oven 5-8 minutes depending on the thickness of the cookies.
Watch carefully as they burn easily.

title: Sandbakkels
instructions: Cream butter and powdered sugar together. Add remaining ingredients.
Chill dough overnight.
Form into tins and bake at 375 degrees for 10 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool a minute or two before turning tart pan over on a cooling rack.
The tart should slide out but sometimes a tap with a spoon on the bottom of pan will loosen.

title: Sandbakkels
instructions: Mix together, then chill.
Use Sandbakkel cookie tins or other small cookie molds such as small tartlet pans.
Press chunks of dough into the bottoms and sides of each mold.
Bake at 350 for 10-12 minutes.

title: Sandbakkels
instructions: Cream shortening, butter and sugar. Add egg and extract. Add the flour to make a stiff dough.
Pinch off small amount of dough. Place in center of tin and with the thumb press dough evenly on inside of sandbakkel tin.
Place filled tins on cookie sheet.
Bake in moderate oven (375˚) for 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Cool before removing from tins. To remove from tin, invert tin and tap gently.
Clean tins with dry cloth only.
Geneva uses butter flavored Crisco and bakes at 350˚ for 15 minutes.

title: Scandinavian Almond Cake
instructions: Use almond cake pan. Spray pan with Pam or cooking spray.
Beat well: sugar, egg, almond extract, and milk.
Add flour, baking powder, and melted butter. Mix well.
Bake at 350 for 40-50 minutes. Edges must be golden brown.
Cool in pan before removing. Cake will break if removed too soon.
Sprinkle with confectionery sugar.
Variation: Before pouring batter into the pan, sprinkle sliced almonds on the bottom.

title: Oslo Kringle (Oslo Pastry)

ingredients.note: for icing, just enough for spreading consistency

instructions: Mix flour and butter; add cold water and mix as for pie crust. Put on cookie sheet in two long strips, two inches wide and 1/2 inch thick.
For cream puff paste: Bring water and butter to boil. Remove from stove and immediately add all flour; stir until smooth.
Add one egg at a time, beating well after each addition. Add flavoring.
Spread on the above strips and bake at 350˚ for 45 minutes.
Frost when cool with following icing: Mix confectioners sugar, butter and almond. Add just enough cream for spreading consistency.
Spread or push through decorating tube.
This is best eaten the same day, but freezes well.

title: Berlinerkranser (Berlin Wreaths)
instructions: Mash the hard cooked yolks and mix in raw yolks. When smooth stir in sugar.
Knead in alternately the butter and flour. Chill the dough overnight.
Break dough into pieces the size of small walnuts; then roll into "ropes" 1/3 – 1/2 inch thick.
Cut into 4-5 inch lengths and form wreaths, overlapping ends. Press down lightly to make ends stick together.
Brush each one with beaten egg white and dip in pearl sugar (crushed loaf sugar).
Bake at 325 degrees for 20 minutes.

title: Rosettes
instructions: Combine flour and milk in a bowl and blend well. Add sugar, salt and vanilla. Lastly add the eggs and beat only until blended.
Heat Crisco oil in deep fat fryer to 375˚ and lower clean rosette iron into hot oil roughly 1 minute.
Blot excess oil from iron onto paper towel and dip iron into batter being careful not to let batter flow over top of iron.
Lower the iron with batter into the hot oil and cook until rosette is golden brown.
Take out of oil, use fork to assist rosette off iron and drain well on paper towels.
Dip cooled rosette into granulated sugar. Store in airtight container. May be frozen.
Optional: Place finished rosettes on a cookie sheet with paper towels and place in a 225˚ oven for 25 minutes. This draws out some of the oil resulting in a crisper rosette.

title: Rosettes with Cloudberry Cream
instructions: Whisk eggs, sugar, and milk lightly together. Sift flour into mixture and stir. Add the melted butter, mixing well.
Refrigerate 30 minutes.
Heat the shortening or oil to 350 degrees F. Heat the rosette iron in the fat.
Dip the iron into the batter. The batter should just reach the top of the iron, not over it.
Deep fry in the fat until just stiff, about 1 minute.
Remove the rosette with a fork and drain on paper towels.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar or fill with cream or jam.
For cloudberry cream: Lightly whip the cream. Fold in the berries, which should be a little too sweet. Add additional sugar, if necessary.
Serve in individual bowls. Top with fresh or sugared cloudberries and serve with almond cookies or rosettes.

title: Goro
instructions: Beat eggs, add sugar and blend thoroughly.
Add cream, melted butter, and dry ingredients and mix well.
Drop a level teaspoon of dough on each pattern of heated iron.
Turn iron to bake the other side.
After removing goro, cut in thirds while warm (a pizza cutter works well).
Store in airtight container.

title: Krumkaker
instructions: Mix together and bake in a Krumkake iron.

title: Krumkaker
instructions: Beat eggs and sugar. Add cooled butter; then flavorings.
Sift flour and cornstarch and add to egg mixture.
Use one good teaspoon on griddle and bake.
These are to be used in electric iron. Squeeze handle together tight so they get thinner.

title: Krumkaker
instructions: Cream sugar and butter. Add eggs.
Add flour mixture of flour and baking powder alternately with milk. Add flavoring. Mix well.
Heat krumkake iron. Place 1 teaspoon batter in center of iron and bake till delicately brown.
Quickly roll cookie on wooden spindle. Let cool.
Store in dry place. A metal tin works well.

title: Scandinavian Almond Bars
contributor: Taste of Home magazine (submitted by Karen Fried)
instructions: In large bowl, cream sugar and butter until light and fluffy. Beat in egg and extract.
Combine the dry ingredients; add to creamed mixture and mix well.
Divide dough into fourths; form into 12" x 3" rectangles.
Place 3" apart on greased baking sheets. Brush with milk; sprinkle with almonds.
Bake at 325˚ for 18-20 minutes or until firm to the touch and edges are lightly browned.
Cool on pans for 5 minutes, then cut diagonally into 1" slices. Remove to wire racks to cool completely.
For icing: In small bowl, combine confectioners sugar, extract and enough milk to achieve desired consistency, drizzle over the bars.

title: Heartshorn Cookies

ingredients.note: in 1 cup warm half and half

instructions: Cream sugar and lard. Add beaten eggs.
Add heartshorn dissolved in the 1 cup warm half & half.
Stir in flour, salt and flavoring.
Roll out, not too thin. Cut with cookie cutter. Sprinkle with red sugar.
Bake at 450 degrees about 5 minutes.

title: Ingelfarkager (Ginger Cookies)
contributor: Fru Else Elisabeth Koren (submitted by Janet Fossum)

ingredients.note: enough to roll out dough very thin

instructions: Melt lard and mix with molasses while hot.
Add other ingredients and roll out thin.
Bake fast, take out of oven while still soft.
Keeps long. This cookie has a shelf life of several months. Store in a cool dry place or freeze.

title: My Favorite Doughnuts
instructions: Heat 3-4 inches canola oil to 375 degrees.
Measure 1 1/2 cup flour and the remaining ingredients into a large mixer bowl.
Blend 1/2 minute on low speed, then beat 2 min at medium speed scraping bowl occasionally.
Stir in remaining flour.
Roll dough gently 3/8 inch thick. Cut with a floured cutter.
With a wide spatula, slide doughnuts into hot oil.
Turn as they rise to the surface. Fry 2-3 min or until golden brown on both sides.
Carefully remove from fat - drain on a rack.
Serve plain, frosted, or mix cinnamon & sugar together and shake in a bag.

title: Smultringers (Doughnuts)
contributor: Angie Reynolds (submitted by Janet Fossum & Kait Peterson)
instructions: Prepare potatoes. Beat eggs, sugar and shortening together; stir in potatoes; beat until blended.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt and mace together; blend into egg mixture.
Chill 1 hour.
Roll out dough on floured board until it is 1/4 inch thick. Cut with doughnut press.
Fry in hot fat (375˚) until golden brown.
Drain on absorbent paper towels.

title: Doughnuts
instructions: Beat eggs well (5 min). Beat in sugar, melted butter and buttermilk.
Sift together 3 cups flour, soda, baking powder, nutmeg & salt. Stir into first mixture.
Add remaining 1/2 cup flour. Chill 1/2 hour.
Roll out on well floured board and cut.
Fry in lard at 370˚.

title: Fattigmann (Poor Man's Cookie)

ingredients.item: flour or a little more to make a soft dough

instructions: Beat eggs, add extracts and salt and mix well.
Stir in flour to make a soft dough. Handle as little as possible.
Roll out on a floured cloth and cut into 3" x 3" diamond shapes with a pastry cutter.
Fry in hot lard (350˚) until lightly browned.
Drain on paper towels and dust with powdered sugar when cool.
Store in airtight container.

title: Fattigmann (Poor Man's Cookies)
instructions: Beat egg whites. Add yolks, butter and sugar.
Add cream, flavoring and stir in flour.
Roll thin, cut into diamond shape.
Cut slit in one point and pull end through the slit.
Fry in hot oil (about 375 to 400 degrees).
Roll in powdered sugar.

title: Mandel-vann bakkel
instructions: Mix flour, butter and water as for pie crust. Pat thin on a cookie sheet in two 12 x 4 inch strips or pat into a round circle on a pizza pan leaving the center open.
Using Part II ingredients, bring to a boil water and butter. Then add all at once the flour. Stir until smooth.
Add flavorings. Add the eggs one at a time and beat well after each.
Spread over pastry mixture and bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour. Be sure to bake it long enough.
Frost with powdered sugar, butter, vanilla and almond extract. Add a small amount of hot water and beat until spreading consistency.

title: Potete Kake
instructions: Put potatoes in mixing bowl. Add butter, sugar, oats and extract. Mix well.
On greased cookie sheet shape dough about size of a dinner plate.
Bake at 325˚ until light brown, about 45 minutes.
Cool and glaze.
For glaze: Mix confectioners sugar, boiling water, and vanilla.

title: Swedish Raspberry Almond Bars
instructions: Cream together butter, powdered sugar, and flour. Pat lightly into a 9x13 pan and bake for 18-20 min at 350 degrees.
Spread raspberry jam on top of first layer.
Beat egg whites until soft peaks, beat in sugar until stiff peaks.
Fold in coconut & 1/2 cup almonds. Spread over jam.
Sprinkle with the other 1/2 cup almonds.
Bake at 350 degrees for 18-22 min until golden.
Sprinkle with more powdered sugar when cool.
Cut into pieces 1 inch x 2 inches.

title: Rømmegrøt Bars
instructions: Grease 9x13 inch pan.
Beat together cream cheese, 1 cup sugar, egg yolk, vanilla, & almond extract.
Press 1 roll of crescent rolls on bottom of pan.
Spread cream cheese mixture on top.
Place second roll of rolls on top of mixture.
Beat egg white until fluffy. Spread over top.
Mix 1/3 cup sugar & 1/2 tsp cinnamon and sprinkle over egg white.
Bake at 350º for 25 to 30 minutes.
Let cool, cut into bars.

title: Cardamom Sugar Cookies
instructions: In a large bowl, cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy - beat in egg and vanilla.
Combine the flour, cardamom, salt and nutmeg, add gradually to the creamed mixture.
Divide in half and shape each portion into a ball, then flatten into a disk.
Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 1/2 hour, until firm.
On a lightly floured surface, roll one portion of dough into 1/8 inch thickness.
Cut with your favorite cutter - place 2" apart on a greased baking sheet.
Bake at 325 degrees for 12-15 minutes or until edges are lightly browned.
Cool for 5 min. before removing from pans to wire racks.
Frost with glaze: Mix confectioners' sugar with 1-2 Tbs milk.
Add coarse sugar and/or edible glitter.

title: Seterjentas Kake (Dairymaid's Wafer)

ingredients.note: leave out a little for rolling

instructions: Have butter at room temperature, stir together with sour cream.
Add remaining ingredients, leaving out a little flour for rolling out the dough.
Knead into a fairly firm dough. Chill for two hours.
Sprinkle a little sugar on top and roll into the dough.
Cut out wafers using a cardboard template the size of Krumkake Iron or use a cookie cutter.
Trace and cut wafers from pattern.
Bake on heated krumkake iron until nice golden color.

title: Kransekake

ingredients.note: not stiff peaks, but so they hold together

instructions: In a bowl mix ground almonds and powdered sugar together. Stir in egg whites.
Continue mixing together until sugar and almonds are all incorporated.
Knead on hard surface for approx. 5 minutes. (can use a little powdered sugar to prevent sticking.)
Wrap dough in plastic, you do not want it to dry out.
Prepare your pans. Grease thoroughly, dust with Cream of Wheat.
Make ropes of dough and put in pans.
Bake at 300-325 until light golden. 12-17 minutes. Let cool, take out of pans.
For icing: whisk one egg white, (can use Wiltons egg powder), add 1/4 tsp vinegar and 1/2 to 1 cup of powdered sugar.
Assemble cake. Put icing in decorator bag with #2 or #3 piping tube.
Start with largest cake ring, make decorative loops of icing, place next size ring on top, decorate that, continue on up.
Cake is eaten by lifting it up, dropping off the bottom layer, and breaking it into pieces.

title: Microwave Rømmegrøt
instructions: In 2-quart casserole or dish, melt margarine on high (1 to 1 1/2 minutes).
Stir in flour, sugar and salt.
In 4-cup measuring cup, microwave milk on HIGH until hot (4-5 minutes).
Whisk hot milk into flour mixture; mix well.
Microwave on HIGH, whisking every 2 minutes, until thickened (8-11 minutes).
Serve warm with melted butter and cinnamon and sugar.

title: Microwave Rømmegrøt

ingredients.item: whole milk or part half & half

instructions: Heat milk in a 1 qt. Pyrex bowl.
In a 2 quart Pyrex bowl, heat butter until melted.
Combine butter with flour, sugar, and salt. Mix well.
Add the milk slowly.
Cook for about 5 minutes on high, then on a lower setting for another 10 minutes.
Stir several times so it doesn't get lumpy.
Serve with butter, sugar & Watkins cinnamon!! So simple and it will not burn!

title: Rømmegrøt
instructions: Melt margarine.
Mix flour, sugar, and salt. Add to the melted margarine.
Heat milk (2% or whole). Add to the rest.
Heat and stir until smooth and thickens.
Serve warm with cinnamon and sugar.

title: Microwave Rømmegrøt
instructions: Melt butter in microwave safe bowl. Stir in flour.
In a separate bowl heat milk on high for 4-5 minutes.
Add milk to flour mixture.
Microwave for 2 to 2 1/2 minute intervals, stirring in between, until moderately thick.
Let cool a bit and then add salt and sugar. Will thicken as it cools.
Serve with melted butter, cinnamon and sugar.

title: Rømmegrøt

ingredients.item: melted butter and cinnamon and sugar

instructions: Heat milk in saucepan.
In a separate pan, melt butter. Add flour, stir with whisk. Cook about 5 minutes, stirring continuously.
Pour in warmed milk, continue stirring until mixture comes to a boil and thickens.
Stir in sugar and salt.
Serve warm with melted butter and cinnamon and sugar.

title: Rømmegrøt
instructions: Boil cream for some time, stirring to keep from scorching.
Gradually add flour stirring until the butter comes out of the cream.
Skim off butter, set aside.
Add milk until smooth.
Serve with melted butter, cinnamon and sugar.
To approximate the taste of Norwegian romme, add some sour cream to the whipping cream.

title: Rømmegrøt
instructions: Melt butter. Add flour and cook 5 minutes.
Heat whole milk and half & half to boiling point.
Add all at once to the flour and butter mixture; bring to a boil.
Add 1/2 cup sugar. Cook for 2 minutes.
Stir frequently to prevent scorching.
Pour into serving bowl. Pour melted butter on top.
Serve warm with sugar and cinnamon.

title: Søtsuppes (Fruit Soup)

ingredients.note: may substitute with pearl tapioca; if so, soak overnight and cook before adding

instructions: Combine all ingredients except apple cubes in 3-quart saucepan. Add 6 cups water.
Bring to a boil stirring. Reduce heat and simmer covered 20 minutes, or until fruit is tender and tapioca is cooked. Stir occasionally.
Add apple cubes. Simmer, covered, 5 more minutes.
Remove cinnamon. Serve warm or cold.

title: Sweet Soup

ingredients.note: optional: apples, tropical mix, blueberries, cranberries, pineapple, etc

instructions: Stir together all of the ingredients in a large pan, such as a roaster, or a roaster lining. Do not cover.
Bake in oven 325˚ for 3-5 hours.
Every 30-45 minutes slowly stir.
Bake until juice is clear.

title: Frukt Soup
instructions: Cook the tapioca in water until transparent.
Add raisins and prunes. Cook until tender.
Add sugar (optional), turn off heat, add grape juice.
Geneva uses 1 12 oz. Welch's Grape Juice Concentrate.
Frukt suppe is called "Bubble Soup" by Geneva's grandchildren because of the large pearl tapioca.

title: Sweet Soup
instructions: Soak tapioca in 5 cups water overnight or four hours.
Cook in double boiler 3 hours until clear.
In separate saucepan, cook prunes, raisins and stick cinnamon in 1 1/2 cups water for 20 minutes. Set aside.
When tapioca is almost clear, combine with cooked raisins and prunes.
Add juice, sugar, salt and lemon juice.
Let stand at least 1/2 hour and cool to warm.
Remove stick cinnamon before serving.

title: Søt Suppe – Sweet Soup
instructions: Cover pitted prunes with water and soak several hours.
Add raisins and let soak while you prepare the following:
Mix together in large saucepan: cold water, grape juice, minute tapioca, sugar, and salt.
Cook until clear.
Add juice of 1 lemon; add juice of 1 large orange.
Add prune, raisin and water mixture.
Cook until prunes and raisins are tender, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Add some more grape juice (Welch's is best).

title: Norwegian Waffles

ingredients.note: butter and gjetost, berries, sour cream, whipped cream, syrup, peanut butter, jam

instructions: Separate eggs. Beat egg whites until stiff. Mix in 1 Tbsp. sugar. Set aside.
In separate large bowl, mix egg yolks and buttermilk.
Sift together flour, baking soda, remaining 2 Tbsp. sugar and salt. Sift again and add to buttermilk mix.
Add melted butter. Fold in egg whites.
Bake on waffle iron.
Some like butter and thin slices of gjetost (Norwegian brown cheese) on their waffles; also berries, sour cream, whipped cream, syrup, even peanut butter and jam.

title: Vafler (Norwegian Waffles)

ingredients.note: thin slices of geitost (goat cheese) or sour cream and raspberry jam

instructions: Combine all ingredients in a bowl.
Bake in waffle iron (traditionally in an iron with heart-shaped sections).
Serve at room temperature with thin slices of geitost (goat cheese) or a dollop of sour cream and raspberry jam.

title: Norwegian Pancakes (Pannekaken)

ingredients.note: fresh berries, syrup or lingonberry jam

instructions: Lightly mix eggs and milk in blender. Add flour, sugar and salt and blend until smooth and no lumps remain.
Heat pan over medium-high heat. Coat pan with butter or cooking spray.
Add 1/4 cup of pancake batter. Tilt pan to coat evenly with batter.
Cook until the top of the pancake looks dry, roughly 30 seconds.
Use spatula to carefully flip the pancake and cook for a few seconds on the other side until browned.
Roll and serve with your favorite topping of fresh berries, syrup or lingonberry jam.

title: Waffle Cookies

ingredients.note: for frosting, to thicken as desired

instructions: Melt chocolate and butter.
In different bowl, beat eggs and sugar. Fold in flour and vanilla.
Mix in melted chocolate and butter.
Drop by teaspoon onto heated heart waffle iron.
Start timing (1 minute) as soon as cover is down. Cool and frost.
For frosting: Melt 1 square chocolate (or 2 tbsp cocoa), brown sugar, water, and butter.
Boil 2 1/2 minutes, add vanilla. Cool and add powdered sugar to thicken as desired.
Can put nuts on top of cookies.

title: Potato Dumplings or Kumla

ingredients.item: ham shank or leftover ham with bone

instructions: Cook ham shank in boiling water until it falls from the bones, 2-3 hours. You can remove ham at this point to make more room for the dumplings.
Mix remaining ingredients with your hands.
When mixed well, clean off your hands and keep wet while making dumplings, about the size of a walnut, packing firmly.
Drop them in the boiling broth and cook gently for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Stir occasionally to prevent dumplings from sticking to bottom of kettle.
Remove dumplings from broth and serve with the cut-up ham.
To reheat leftovers: Keep leftovers in the broth and reheat that way. Can also remove them from the broth, slice and fry them in butter.

title: Raspa Kumla (Potato Dumplings)
instructions: Mix potatoes, egg, butter, and salt.
Add enough barley flour or other flour until dough is firm.
Drop by spoonfuls into broth.
Bring to boil, then simmer for 1/2 to 3/4 hour, depending on size.
Ham or pork broth is best.
Stir to keep dumplings from sticking to bottom.

title: Mom's Dumplings for Soup

ingredients.note: about, amount varies depending on size of potatoes and eggs

instructions: Boil 2 medium potatoes in soup broth until done. Remove and mash with a fork.
Add eggs, salt, baking powder, and about 1/2 cup flour to make a dumpling consistency. (Amount of flour varies depending on the size of the potatoes and eggs).
Put in soup broth by small spoonfuls and cook until done, about 15 minutes.
Good in either beef or chicken soup.
These hold together well when reheated.

title: Milk Soup with Dumplings or Klep Suppe
instructions: Combine eggs, 1/4 cup milk, flour, 1/2 tsp salt, baking powder, and sugar. Mix until smooth.
Heat 4 cups milk in microwave for about 5 minutes, add 1 tsp. salt.
Put butter in a heavy pan and melt. Add hot milk.
Drop dumplings by small spoonfuls into milk and cook until done on low to medium heat, about 15 minutes.
Stir frequently so it doesn't scorch.
This is from an old Norwegian cookbook.

title: Lapskaus

ingredients.item: chuck steak, cut into 3/4 inch pieces
large carrots, chopped into 3/4 inch pieces
parsley roots, chopped into 3/4 inch pieces

instructions: Brown batches of meat in a casserole pot with melted butter.
Add meat, chopped vegetables and chicken stock to the pot.
Season as desired with salt and pepper and bring to a boil. Skim top of stew if needed.
Cover with a tight fitting lid and simmer for 2 1/2 hours.
Stir carefully so that vegetables do not break down and become mushy.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. If stew is too dense, thin with stock or water.
Serve in bowls with a sprinkle of parsley and your favorite bread.

title: Lillian's Norwegian Meatballs
instructions: Mix together all ingredients.
Form into balls.
Bake in oven for one hour.

title: Shrimp Dollops
instructions: Bake biscuits per package directions.
Cut biscuits in halves or thirds, and spread them on a cookie sheet.
Mix mayonnaise, Parmesan cheese, shrimp, dry mustard, and onion.
Top each biscuit slice with a dollop of the mixture.
Broil until they bubble. Watch carefully.
Serve hot.

title: Fruit Salad Dressing

ingredients.note: may use more for thicker consistency

instructions: Bring all ingredients to a boil.
Cool, then pour over assorted fresh fruit.

title: Acini di pepe Salad
instructions: Cook, drain and cool Acini di pepe macaroni.
Drain juice from pineapple and mandarin oranges.
Thicken 2 cups juice with sugar, cornstarch and beaten eggs.
Mix thickened juice with macaroni and fruit and let set overnight.
Next day fold in marshmallows and Cool Whip.
Note: this is great to take along when going to a potluck!!

title: Cranberry Salad
instructions: Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Mix unflavored gelatin with orange liquid, then add to jello in boiling water.
Chill until syrupy.
Grind raw cranberries and orange sections.
Blend in sugar and lemon juice. Let stand a few minutes to dissolve sugar.
Stir mixture into jello. Put into quart bowl.

title: Sauerkraut Salad
instructions: Drain sauerkraut. Add celery, onion, green pepper, and black pepper to taste.
For dressing: boil sugar and cider vinegar for 2 minutes.
Cool to room temperature.
Mix dressing with salad and refrigerate overnight.
Keeps well!!

title: Potato Salad Dressing

ingredients.note: or more, dehydrated/reconstituted or peel & slice your own

instructions: Use dehydrated/reconstituted potatoes or peel & slice your own – 5 lb or more.
Cook potatoes for about 20 min. Drain and rinse with cold water. Drain well.
Mix salad dressing, half and half, sugar, mustard, salt and pepper.
Mix potatoes with dressing, some onion to taste, and a dozen chopped hard-boiled eggs.

title: Cheesy Vegetable Soup

ingredients.item: condensed cream of mushroom soup, undiluted

instructions: In a large kettle bring water to a boil. Add hashbrowns, vegetables and bouillon.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer for 10 min. or until vegetables are tender.
Stir in the cheese, soup and milk. Cook and stir until cheese is melted.
Serve immediately or cool and freeze for up to 3 months.
Optional: Add some chopped ham. Also made only 1/2 of the recipe at times.
To use frozen soup: Thaw in refrigerator. Heat in a saucepan, adding additional milk, if desired.

title: Dutch Style Green Beans
instructions: Fry bacon until crisp, remove and crumble.
Drain off all but 1 tablespoon fat, add chopped onion and brown lightly.
Stir in cornstarch, salt and mustard.
Drain beans, reserving 1/2 cup liquid. Add reserved liquid to above ingredients and bring to a boil until slightly thickened.
Blend in brown sugar and vinegar, add drained beans and heat.
Put into serving dish and top with crumbled bacon.
Recipe may easily be doubled.

title: Escalloped Corn
instructions: Mix all ingredients except the additional crushed crackers and parmesan cheese.
Place in a greased oven proof casserole.
Put an additional ¼ C crushed crackers and ¼ C parmesan cheese on top.
Bake 1 hour at 350 degrees.

title: Deb's Meatballs

ingredients.item: fine dry crumbs from seasoned croutons

instructions: Use blender to make 2 C fine dry crumbs from seasoned croutons (Kellogg's).
Add to crumbs in blender: eggs, garlic powder, milk, Tabasco, onion, and salt.
Add to meats and mix with hands until thoroughly combined.
Shape into 48 meatballs.
Bake at 400 degrees for 30 minutes.

title: Gravy
instructions: Cook butter, drippings, flour, salt, and beef stock until smooth.
Add Kitchen Bouquet if desired.

title: Pickled Pig's Feet
instructions: Cook pig's feet or pork hocks a couple of hours in water to cover, until tender.
Add bay leaf and salt to water before cooking.
Remove hocks to a covered bowl.
For pickling solution: Boil broth, white vinegar, salt, sugar, and pickling spice (in a bag) for a couple of minutes.
Pour pickling solution over hocks.
Let stand for at least two days before eating.
If over 4# of hocks are cooked, you may need to double pickling solution.

title: Curried Rice
instructions: Dice up and fry about 1 to 2 cups ham with about 1/3 cup diced onion.
Add about 1 jar of canned tomatoes (1 qt.).
Stir and break up the big pieces.
Add 1 1/2 tsp curry powder, to taste.
Cook about 20 minutes on low, stirring occasionally.
Add about 2 cups cooked rice and cook 10 more minutes.

title: Southern Biscuits
instructions: Heat oven to 450 degrees.
Mix dry ingredients in food processor or by hand.
Add shortening, pulse until mixture looks like meal.
Add just enough buttermilk to make a soft, easy to roll dough.
Knead 20-25 times.
Roll a little less than ½" thick, cut and place on ungreased baking sheet.
Bake 10-12 minutes.
These are more tender than regular baking powder biscuits. Great with sausage gravy.

title: Sausage Gravy
instructions: Brown sausage and onion.
Add flour, salt & pepper.
Cook 2-3 minutes.
Add milk, cook 3-4 minutes.
Serve with baking powder biscuits.

title: Never Fail Scalloped Potatoes
instructions: Mix sliced potatoes and onions together in casserole dish.
Melt butter, add flour.
Add milk, bring to a boil, stirring until thickened.
Add salt and pepper.
Pour over potatoes and bake 350 degrees for 1 hour covered.
Then bake 30 minutes uncovered.
Make sure there is enough sauce to cover the potatoes. (Depending on potatoes, it may take longer to bake until done.)

title: Gracie's Cabbage Hot Dish

ingredients.item: raw medium potato pared & coarsely shredded

instructions: Heat oven to 350 ˚.
Melt butter in skillet with onion salt.
Brown hamburger in this.
Put hamburger mixture to one side, add 3 cups cabbage so it wilts (cover) then mix with hamburger.
Add raw potato and rest of cabbage.
Mix all & add milk.
Cover until wilted (2-5 minutes).
Put in casserole and top with cheese.
Cover. Bake until cheese melts (about 1/2 hour).
Can vary meat and cabbage amounts. Variation- omit potato, milk and maybe cheese. Add can of tomato soup instead. Salt & pepper to taste.

title: Peanut Butter Pie

ingredients.item: Two pie shells or chocolate, or graham cracker crusts

instructions: Mix cream cheese, sugar, peanut butter and milk.
When well mixed, fold in Cool Whip.
Pour into two pie shells or chocolate, or graham cracker crusts; chill.
Freezes well.
Recipe received from a relative, Jan Mc Tier, in Dearing, GA.

title: Zucchini Fudge Cake
instructions: In a large bowl beat eggs until fluffy.
Add sugar gradually, beating until mixture is thick and lemon-colored.
Beat in vanilla and butter.
Combine flour, cocoa, baking powder, soda and salt.
Stir ½ of dry ingredients into egg mixture.
Add buttermilk; mix.
Add remaining flour mix, zucchini and nuts.
Divide batter into a Bundt pan or 4 8 or 9 inch round greased and floured pans.
Bake Bundt cake 45 min – 1 hour, round ones 25-30 min or until top springs back when gently pressed.
Cool in pans 10 minutes, remove to wire racks and cool completely.
Make frosting by combining butter, powdered sugar, cocoa, vanilla, and milk in a large bowl, beat until creamy.
Frost cake. Yield 20 large servings.

title: Pretzel Snax
instructions: Mix together and spread out on cookie sheets.
Bake at 300˚ for 30 minutes stirring every 10 minutes.
Let cool and bag.

title: Cornflake Cookies
instructions: Combine all ingredients.
Bake 8-10 minutes at 350˚.
Makes a large batch.

title: Rhubarb Custard Bars

ingredients.item: finely chopped fresh or frozen rhubarb, thawed and drained

instructions: Combine flour and sugar, cut in butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Press into a greased 9x13 baking pan.
Bake at 350 degrees for 10 minutes.
For filling: Combine sugar and flour. Whisk in whipping cream and eggs.
Stir in chopped rhubarb.
Pour over crust.
Bake at 350 for 40-45 minutes or until custard is set.
Cool.
For topping: Beat together cream cheese, sugar, and vanilla until smooth.
Fold in whipped cream.
Spread over top.
Cover and chill. Store in the refrigerator.

title: Oatmeal Cake
instructions: Combine oatmeal and boiling water, cool.
Mix sugars with butter.
Add eggs and cooled oatmeal mixture to sugar and butter mixture.
Sift together flour, salt, soda, cinnamon, and baking powder.
Add to wet ingredients.
Bake at 350 for 45 minutes in a 9x13 pan.
For topping: Mix butter, brown sugar, cream, coconut, walnuts, and vanilla.
Spread on warm cake.
Put under broiler 4" from heat for 2 ½ minutes or bake for 10 more minutes.

title: Ginger Snaps
instructions: Beat together Crisco, white sugar, egg, and molasses.
Sift together salt, flour, soda, cloves, ginger, and cinnamon.
Beat dry ingredients into wet mixture.
Make balls size of walnut.
Roll in white sugar.
Press down.
Bake moderate oven.

title: Edith's White Sugar Cookies

ingredients.note: can also add almond or other flavors

instructions: Cream sugars and butter.
Add oil and eggs - beat well.
Sift together flour, salt, cream of tarter, and baking soda.
Add sifted dry ingredients and mix well.
Chill dough.
Roll into balls and place on cookie sheet and press with a glass dipped in sugar.
Bake at 350 degrees for 10-15 minutes.
Yield 5 dozen.
You can decorate with colored or pearl sugar for the holidays or you can add 1/2 cup cocoa for chocolate cookies.
Mom keeps these on hand all the time as they are the grandchildrens' favorite.

title: Rarebit
instructions: Melt butter.
Add flour.
Continue heating, add milk.
Add Velveeta cheese.
Melt altogether.
Cut up and add olives.
Serve over crackers or toast. Also good on a baked potato.

title: Almond Bark Clumps
instructions: Melt almond bark and peanut butter.
Stir in peanuts, marshmallows, and Rice Krispies.
Drop by clumps onto wax paper.
Let cool.

title: Banana Bread
instructions: Cream sugar & Crisco.
Add beaten eggs, salt, soda, and bananas (which have been crushed).
Then add flour.
Fill one bread loaf pan.
Bake one hour at 350˚.

title: Mom's Oatmeal Rolls
instructions: Combine hot water, oatmeal, margarine, brown sugar, and salt.
Cook for 1 minute - cool.
In another bowl combine yeast, warm water, and white sugar.
Combine mixtures and add 4 3/4 - 5 1/4 cup flour. The best rolls have the least amount of flour.
Knead 6-8 minutes.
Cover and let raise until doubled.
Punch down & let rest 10 minutes.
Shape into 18 balls and put into 2 9" round pans.
Raise until double.
Bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes.
Note: for dark rolls, substitute molasses for brown sugar.
